name: Rocky Mountain Circuits
old_description: Rocky Mountain Circuits is a printed circuit board manufacturer in Longmont, Colorado, specializing in quick-turn PCBs with multi-layer boards up to 24 layers, filled and buried vias, and RoHS-compliant materials, serving industrial automation, medical electronics, and wireless communication customers.
about:
Rocky Mountain Circuits operates from Longmont, Colorado, where it has fabricated printed circuit boards since 1972. The company is privately held; no specific ownership designation such as family-, veteran-, or woman-owned is disclosed in its public materials.

The shop produces double-sided through 24-layer multilayer boards, including rigid, flex, and rigid-flex constructions. Processes cover blind and buried vias, filled vias, sequential lamination, microvias, controlled-depth milling, backdrilling, and impedance modeling with 3-mil line/space capability. Surface finishes include HASL (lead-free and standard), ENIG, and immersion silver. Materials range from standard FR4 to high-frequency Rogers, Taconic, Nelco, and Teflon substrates, plus aluminum-based boards for thermal management. The facility also assembles custom cable harnesses and provides box-build integration, offering a prototype-to-production flow with quick-turn options as fast as 48 hours and standard leads of 10 days. Offshore partners handle higher-volume runs.

Customers span medical devices, industrial automation, automotive electronics, consumer products, semiconductor test, Internet of Things, energy systems, and network/telecommunications infrastructure. The company cites work in each of these sectors on its website.

Rocky Mountain Circuits attributes its longevity to a philosophy of building high-quality product, delivering on time, and pricing competitively. It emphasizes rapid turnaround, UL-approved material compliance, and a one-stop model that includes fabrication, assembly, cable, and box-build services.

name: S&K Electronics, Inc.
old_description: S&K Electronics, Inc. is a premier, tribally-owned electronics contract manufacturer founded in 1984 by the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes (CSKT), operating from a modern 42,000-square-foot facility in Ronan, Montana on the Flathead Indian Reservation. Specializing in high-reliability circuit card assembly (SMT and Through-Hole), custom wire harnesses, and electromechanical box builds, S&K Electronics serves mission-critical aerospace, defense, medical, and industrial sectors. Certified to AS9100D, ISO 9001 compliant, and ITAR registered with IPC-A-610 Class 3 workmanship standards, the company delivers end-to-end manufacturing solutions from prototyping and precision machining to automated testing, conformal coating, and turnkey production.
about:
S&K Electronics, Inc. was founded in 1984 by the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes on the Flathead Indian Reservation in Ronan, Montana. The tribally-owned company operates from a 42,000-square-foot facility spanning three buildings in the Mission Valley.

The contract manufacturer specializes in high-reliability circuit card assembly using surface-mount and through-hole technologies, custom wire harnesses, and electromechanical box builds. Its capabilities extend to automated optical inspection, flying probe and in-circuit testing, 2D/3D X-ray inspection, conformal coating, and an in-house precision machine shop. The facility supports high-mix, low-to-high volume turnkey production with a workforce of 51 to 200 employees.

S&K serves aerospace and defense prime contractors, medical equipment makers, industrial automation firms, telecommunications companies, and energy sector clients. The company is ITAR registered and holds AS9100D certification, making it a qualified supplier for mission-critical defense and aerospace programs.

The business was established to create economic opportunity for the tribal community while delivering quality-driven electronics manufacturing. S&K emphasizes financially stable operations, 100% inspection and testing, and adherence to IPC Class 3 workmanship standards as key differentiators.

Its core services include custom cable assembly, wire harnessing, electro-mechanical assembly (box build), lead wire assembly, cordsets, wire and cable processing, engineering support for new product introduction and design for manufacturing, and testing for performance, safety, and compliance. The shop performs certified soldering and crimping, crimp height verification, crimp pull testing, hipot testing, and computerized testing, supported by tooling calibration, machine maintenance, and statistical process control reporting.

SHINE serves medical device manufacturers such as Smith Medical, along with other electronics and industrial customers requiring UL/CSA-compliant cordsets and RoHS-compliant assemblies. The company emphasizes a blend of engineering resources, account management, and a vetted global supply chain, positioning itself as a quality-driven contract manufacturer. SHINE is a member of the Wire Harness Manufacturers Association and contributed to the development of the IPC-620 standard, reflecting its commitment to industry standards.

SMC Integration Solutions, LLC was founded in 1996 in Nicholasville, Kentucky. The privately held company operates two facilities in the heart of Kentucky, serving the technology industry in the eastern region.

The company provides electronic manufacturing services (EMS) and systems integration, including printed circuit board assembly, custom cable and wire harness assembly, complex box build, and full assembly testing. Its capabilities span new product introduction (NPI) and rapid prototyping through low-, medium-, and high-volume production. SMC maintains five dedicated engineering groups—customer, test, process, quality, and systems integration—supported by a strategic business management function. SMC emphasizes a partnership model built on its “4 P’s”—Principles, People, Process, and Performance—and offers direct fulfillment to end customers. Differentiators cited by the company include an electronic 8D corrective-action system integrated with its ERP, a manufacturing execution system tailored for EMS, and in-house development of test systems to ensure product reliability.

name: SMK Packaging
old_description: SMK Packaging is a vertically integrated low cost manufacturer of high quality custom-made flexible packaging with focus on the highly competitive fast-paced fresh produce market segment in the western USA.
about:
SMK Packaging was founded in 2011 by Steven Karlsrud in Reno, Nevada. The privately held company began as a vertically integrated operation focused on producing custom flexible packaging for the fast‑paced fresh produce market in the western United States.

The company controls the full production chain in‑house: blown film extrusion using three‑layer coextrusion and six‑component gravimetric dosing, prepress services including design, trapping, bar coding and plate making, printing on two eight‑color central impression flexographic presses capable of 50‑inch web width, and converting that produces wicketed bags, side‑weld bags, roll stock with vent holes, zippers and handle features. An on‑site laboratory performs OTR, tensile, dart, seal strength, haze, gloss, density and melt‑flow testing on resins, films and finished goods.

SMK primarily serves fresh‑produce packers and other food‑contact packaging customers across the western U.S., and is expanding into additional markets that require short lead times and responsive service. Its packaging is designed for vertical and horizontal form‑fill‑seal equipment used in automated and hand‑pack lines.

The business was built on a vision of responsiveness and vertical integration, aiming to eliminate bottlenecks by keeping every step under one roof. Management emphasizes flexibility — offering rush orders and custom film structures without long queue times — and maintains GMP and HACCP programs audited by third parties to ensure safety for direct food contact.

name: Sea Watch International Ltd
old_description: Sea Watch International is a seafood company based in the Chesapeake Bay region of Maryland and has been a major supplier of clams for over 35 years. The company was founded in 1978 in Milford, Delaware. Sea Watch is proud to be recognized as the largest harvester and processor of clam products in the world. All of our clams are harvested in US fishing waters under US Federal regulations by US flagged vessels. Sea Watch has taken its place as the leader in the offshore clam industry and positioned itself as one of the top seafood companies in the US.
about:
Sea Watch International Ltd was founded in 1978 in Milford, Delaware, and operates from its headquarters in Easton, Maryland, on the Chesapeake Bay. The company remains independently owned, with ownership actively involved in daily operations alongside experienced department heads. It began as a clam harvesting and processing venture and has grown into a vertically integrated seafood enterprise.

The company harvests surf clams and ocean quahogs using a fleet of 30 to 34 U.S.-flagged vessels in federal waters. Processing occurs across four state-of-the-art plants in Maryland, Delaware, Maine, and Massachusetts, with a co-packing facility in Virginia. These plants produce frozen and canned clam products—chowder, strips, nuggets, sauces, chopped clams, juice, stuffed clams, and concentrates—plus value-added items such as crab cakes, breaded calamari, tempura shrimp, and Super Surfer clam strips. The Milford plant is USDA and Kosher approved for soup production. Co-packing services include custom formula development, canning, portion-pack bagging, zip-locking, and klik-locking, all under HACCP and BRC-certified quality systems.

Sea Watch serves a national base of commercial and non-commercial foodservice customers, acts as a major industrial and national-brand co-pack supplier, and supplies many of the top 100 U.S. chain restaurants. An export division handles international sales, and products are also sold through retail channels.

The company emphasizes its position as the world’s largest harvester and processor of clam products and the largest independently owned, vertically integrated clam company. It works with the National Marine Fisheries Service under a quota system to manage the fishery sustainably, and its product development team brings more than 30 years of experience to new product creation.

old_description: SeaTac Packaging is an independently owned and professionally operated manufacturing company located in the Greater Seattle area. Founded in 1994, SeaTac Packaging designs, manufactures, and delivers a wide variety of multiwall, PaperWoven™, and flexible packaging. Made in Washington, from our roots serving the seafood industry, SeaTac Packaging has organically grown to be a valued partner for small businesses to Fortune 500 companies by focusing on quality and service at a competitive price. Scroll down to learn more!
about:
SeaTac Packaging Manufacturing Corporation operates from Puyallup, Washington, in the Greater Seattle area. The company was founded in 1994 by Scott, who identified an opportunity to better serve the Pacific Northwest fishing community with an innovative PaperWoven™ product. Starting with three employees, one bag line, and one printing press, the independently owned business set out to become the preferred supplier for seafood processors.

Today, SeaTac designs, manufactures, and delivers a range of multiwall, PaperWoven™, and flexible packaging solutions. Its capabilities span flexographic printing up to ten colors using water-based inks, coating and laminating with structures such as polypropylene, high-density polyethylene, and biaxially oriented polyamide, as well as graphic design, product development, and converting. The company runs multiple bag lines and what it describes as the widest-web, longest-repeat sustainable water-based press in the western United States, supported by large modern warehouses with 30-foot clear heights and high-bay racking for vendor-managed inventory programs.

SeaTac serves industries including food and ingredient packaging (flour, rice, evaporated dairy, potatoes, spices), agricultural products (seed, beans, peas, lentils), chemical products, and its original fishing and seafood sector. Its customer base ranges from small businesses to Fortune 500 companies, with the company emphasizing a local touch backed by a global network.

The firm differentiates itself as a vertically integrated, MBE-certified manufacturer—the only U.S. polyethylene woven producer with that designation, according to its leadership. All bags are made in America at facilities compliant with FSMA and FDA regulations and audited to the GFSI IFS PACsecure higher-level standard. A lean, just-in-time philosophy underpins what the company calls lead times, while an in-house lab and third-party testing partners support quality assurance and food safety commitments.

name: Segue Manufacturing Services LLC
old_description: Lorom, In-Tech Electronics, and Segue Manufacturing Services are now Lisconn — a new name that reflects our shared 100 years of experience in electronics, engineering, and interconnect innovation. Backed by Cornell Capital, Lisconn brings together the expertise of three industry leaders under one trusted brand.
about:
Segue Manufacturing Services operates from North Billerica, Massachusetts, just outside Boston. The company established operations in 1991 with the goal of getting customers' products to market while exceeding expectations. It is a U.S.-owned and operated business backed by private equity firm Cornell Capital. In 2024, Segue joined with Lorom and In-Tech Electronics to form Lisconn, a combined entity reflecting a shared 100 years of experience in electronics, engineering, and interconnect innovation.

As a global contract manufacturer, Segue integrates engineering services with manufacturing operations in Boston, Tijuana (Mexico), and Xiamen (China), plus partner factories in Malaysia and India. The company provides capabilities scaling from sub-assembly level to complete end-to-end manufacturing, including prototype fabrication, new product introduction, domestic stocking and replenishment, and quality systems. Its vertically integrated model combines local engineering and customer service with cost-effective global production.

Segue serves OEMs and Tier 1 electronics manufacturing services customers across highly regulated sectors. Its industry expertise spans medical devices and healthcare, industrial automation and robotics, capital equipment and semiconductor, industrial and IoT, instrumentation, energy and environmental, and aerospace and defense. The company focuses on complex electronic products where it has deep assembly experience.

Segue differentiates itself through right-shoring flexibility, offering customers the benefits of local engineering support combined with manufacturing where it makes economic sense. The company emphasizes proactive customer service, real-time testing systems, and common manufacturing platforms that enable rapid transitions without compromising quality. It only takes on projects where it has the experience to deliver successfully, aiming to lower inventory carrying costs while maintaining exceptional delivery performance.

The company emphasizes flexibility in customizing production to each client’s goals, advanced technology such as ultrasonic seals and real-time process monitoring, and a quality management system validated by third-party audits including SQF. old_description: Sentra-Sota Sheet Metal, Inc. was founded on May 26, 1982 by Ben Bechtold and Jerry Vogt. about:
Sentra-Sota Sheet Metal, Inc. was founded on May 26, 1982, by Ben Bechtold and Jerry Vogt in Waite Park, Minnesota. The name reflects their central Minnesota roots, and the business began in the founders' garages before moving to a dedicated shop on Roosevelt Road in St. Cloud in 1984.

The company operates a full-service custom sheet metal fabrication shop and a dedicated HVAC system fabrication and installation department at its current 3075 3rd Street South facility. Its capabilities cover architectural sheet metal, commercial HVAC ductwork, and custom metal products for projects ranging from large multi-story buildings to single-room installations. As of 1999 the shop employed 27 people; current headcount is not publicly disclosed.

Sentra-Sota serves industrial, manufacturing, commercial property developers, medical facilities, food service, educational facilities, retail outlets, and residential customers throughout central Minnesota. The firm has worked on multiple LEED-registered projects and counts commercial, industrial, and residential buildings among its installed work.

The company emphasizes competitive pricing, quality craftsmanship, and timely turnaround, supported by ongoing safety training and the integration of new fabrication technology. Its longevity and second-generation ownership under Jeff Bechtold, Jeff Popp, and Tyler Bechtold underscore a focus on continuity and customer relationships.

name: Shermco Industries (previously Power Products & Solutions)
old_description: Shermco is North America’s largest and fastest-growing electrical testing organization accredited by the InterNational Electrical Testing Association. Trusted since 1974, Shermco has you covered when it comes to electrical testing, maintenance, and industry requirements.
about:
Shermco Industries, headquartered in Irving, Texas, was founded in 1974 by Pete Sherman. The company began by repairing generators for aircraft during the Vietnam War, with Sherman recalling that at one point nearly every B-52 in the U.S. fleet had a generator serviced by Shermco. That dedication to quality and personal service turned single-job clients into long-term partners, fueling the firm's growth into a nationwide electrical services provider.

Today Shermco operates as an electrical services platform delivering field, shop, and engineering & control services. Its 700-plus NETA-certified technicians and 230-plus engineers work from 41 service centers across the United States and Canada. Core offerings include NETA-accredited power system testing and maintenance, transformer services, protection and control engineering, rotating machinery repair, wind turbine support, motor and generator rewinds up to 15 kV, circuit breaker refurbishment, disaster recovery, and electrical safety training. The motor shops hold ISO 9001:2015 and EASA accreditation, while breaker technicians are PEARL certified.

The company serves data centers, utilities, oil and gas producers, chemical plants, industrial manufacturers, and the growing wind energy sector. Clients in these markets rely on Shermco to maintain continuous operation and avoid downtime, leveraging the firm's expertise in NERC, ERCOT, PJM, and CAISO compliance, interconnection studies, and field engineering support.

Shermco states its purpose is to provide specialty technical expertise that safely and reliably powers essential businesses and communities. It emphasizes a safety-first culture where every employee can stop work without reprisal, and it positions itself as North America's largest and fastest-growing NETA-accredited testing organization.

name: Southeastern Kentucky Rehabilitation Industries
old_description: SEKRI has formed a business relationship with non-profit organization Operation Warm. Founded in 1998, Operation Warm produces coats for children in need across the United States. For the past three years, they have manufactured coats both overseas and in U.S. manufacturing companies. The partnership between SEKRI and Operation Warm was launched in March 2016.
about:
Southeastern Kentucky Rehabilitation Industries (SEKRI) was established in 1971 in Corbin, Kentucky, as a non-profit organization dedicated to creating employment opportunities for people with mental and physical disabilities in the Appalachian region. At a time when few jobs existed for individuals with significant disabilities, government agencies and school systems began referring clients to SEKRI for basic work-skills training.

Today SEKRI operates seven facilities across Kentucky and Tennessee, employing more than 700 people. The organization runs spreading and cutting operations on Gerber equipment and provides a full range of sewing services—from flat-lock single-needle stitching to embroidery—producing military apparel, commercial textiles, and partner products such as coats for Operation Warm. In addition to manufacturing, SEKRI offers contract packaging, fulfillment, warehousing, inventory management, and logistics, shipping over 50,000 units per week from its combined plants. The company also deploys teams to prepare and wrap training-range facilities with site-specific vinyl for military exercises.

SEKRI’s primary customers are federal and defense agencies purchasing through the AbilityOne program, which requires a workforce of at least 75 percent disabled individuals. Key accounts include the U.S. military for sewn goods and Lockheed Martin, for which SEKRI manages vendor‑owned inventory and delivers orders in as little as two hours, earning a Platinum Vendor Supplier Rating. The non-profit also serves commercial partners such as Operation Warm and has supported training-range construction for soldier readiness programs.

SEKRI’s founding mission—to provide competitive, gainful employment for persons with disabilities—remains its central differentiator. The organization maintains ISO 9001:2015 certification and a quality policy targeting 100 percent customer requirements and on-time delivery. Its AbilityOne designation and non-profit structure allow it to reinvest revenue directly into workforce development, including on‑site GED programs, veteran services, and rehabilitation referrals.

Star Plastics, LLC, headquartered in Millwood, West Virginia, traces its origins to 1988 when parent company SDR Plastics was formed as a post-industrial recycling operation. The company specializes in custom color compounding, toll compounding, and polymer sourcing for engineering-grade thermoplastics, with a focus on ABS, polycarbonates, polycarbonate alloys, and nylons. Star also provides recycled-content materials up to 100% classification, including pre-consumer, post-consumer, ITE, and ocean-bound grades. The firm emphasizes batches of any size, supported by over 35 years of tolling experience.

Star serves automotive, electronics/electrical, and hybrid vehicle industries, as well as large resin manufacturers. Its materials are UL-recognized and certified for automotive applications. The PolymerVault division sources and supplies resins of any grade or form globally.

Founded on a mission to reclaim plastic waste, Star differentiates itself through a 98.6% material satisfaction rate over three years, weekly continuous-improvement meetings, and a comprehensive analytical lab capable of Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, and a suite of mechanical and flammability tests.

The company began with two HDPE pipe production lines and expanded to four by 2013. A second state-of-the-art manufacturing facility opened in Albuquerque in 2015, and four additional lines were added across both plants over the following four years. In June 2022, Atkore, Inc. (founded 1959, based in Harvey, IL) acquired United Poly Systems, and the business has since been acquired by Infra Pipe Solutions.

The company manufactures high- and medium-density polyethylene (HDPE/MDPE) pipe and conduit in diameters from 3/4-in. to 26-in. IPS, 4-in. to 24-in. DIPS, and 3/4-in. to 2-in. CTS. In its first decade, United Poly Systems produced over 120,000 miles of pipe. The manufacturing process includes resin quality inspections (cleanliness, carbon black content, melt flow index, density), dimensional testing (diameter, wall thickness, eccentricity, ovality, out-of-round), and tensile property testing (elongation at break, ring tensile burst, quick burst). Products are available in 12 colors with custom striping, packaged in reels, sticks, or coils, and can be customized with ribbed interiors, pull tape, or lubricated interiors.

United Poly Systems serves the broadband and telecommunications, power and communications, oil and gas, and energy utility markets. Customers include telecommunications contractors, broadband providers such as Foothills Broadband, utility district contractors, and electrical/high-voltage infrastructure projects. The company’s product suites — Comm-Line™, MicroPath™, Power-Line™, Pro-Line™, Sleeve-It!™, Hard-Line™, and Cable-in-Conduit — are designed for communications conduit, microduct, electrical conduit, large-diameter PVC replacement, and cable-in-conduit applications.

The company emphasizes its agile business model, coast-to-coast manufacturing footprint that reduces freight costs and lead times, and compliance with the Buy American Act for domestic sourcing. Its quality program covers resin, dimensional, and burst testing to UL, NSF, AWWA, and ASTM standards.

Vesper Medical states its vision is a world free from the pain and disability associated with deep venous disease. Its core values are respect, integrity, innovation, quality, and patients first. Veterans Trading Company (VTC) is headquartered in Ocala, Florida, where its primary Supplier Managed Inventory (SMI) facility operates, with additional presence across seven states. Its customer base includes major primes such as Lockheed Martin, The Boeing Company, Northrop Grumman, and BAE Systems, for whom it designs and manages supply chain models that reduce inventory and floor-space requirements.

The business was built on a “Best In Class” service principle that still drives its quality management system, which employs DMAIC Six Sigma methods across all processes. VTC highlights its ISO 9100:2015 and AS9100D certifications, its veteran-owned status, and a track record of industry awards for innovative supply chain models that deliver measurable productivity gains and cost savings.

Quality is backed by ISO 9001:2015 certification, UL approval for wiring harnesses, and compliance with RoHS, REACH, DFARS/ITAR, and conflict minerals requirements. Washington Metal Fabricators was built on the principle that diverse equipment investment enables the most efficient manufacturing route for each part. By reviewing every aspect of a client’s design, the firm aims to deliver precision, speed to market, and competitive pricing without designing the product itself.

The company specializes in heavy-duty press brake forming with machines ranging from 50 to 1,500 tons, allowing complex parts to be produced in a single piece without splice welding. The firm emphasizes quick turn-around, competitive pricing, and worldwide shipping, positioning its versatility and caring customer service as key differentiators. By consolidating multiple operations under one roof, it aims to reduce assembly time and material waste for clients.

The company manufactures a range of chassis components for racing and off‑road applications, including suspension mounts, shock mounts, engine and transmission mounts, braking hardware, gussets, fasteners, and heim joints. Roughly 90 % of the catalog is produced in‑house using precision stamping, laser cutting, machining, and fabrication; the balance comes from local partners. A single facility houses both production and a walk‑in showroom, and in‑stock orders can ship same‑day nationwide.

Customers include race teams, hot‑rod builders, off‑road enthusiasts, professional technicians, and fabrication shops — anyone who needs weld‑ready components with consistent fitment. The shop also supports DIY racers and technician shops with custom one‑off or short‑run tabs, brackets, and specialty mounts, offering guidance on material selection and design trade‑offs.

A&A emphasizes domestic manufacturing as a differentiator: controlling materials, tolerances, and finish in its own shop yields repeatable hole sizing, bend accuracy, and weld‑ready edges. Local sourcing for the remaining items allows quick scaling of specialty runs without compromising quality, and the team provides responsive support from people who know the parts because they make them.

old_description: Originally a small sheet metal business founded in 1907, AC Horn has developed into a leading global supplier of food processing equipment. PROBAT's investment in this acquisition not only complements its existing products and services, particularly for nut and snack processing, but also increases the efficiency of its own production processes through greater vertical integration. about:
AC Horn Manufacturing traces its roots to a modest garage in Dallas, Texas, where the company was founded in 1907 as a small sheet metal operation. The business took its modern shape in 1946 when A.C. 'Ace' Horn assumed leadership of his father's enterprise, establishing a philosophy built on integrity and keeping one's word. The company remains family-owned, with Michael Horn serving as president and CEO until its acquisition by Germany's PROBAT Group in February 2024.

Today, Horn designs and builds processing equipment for the snack food industry, including popcorn cookers and coaters, continuous and batch nut roasters, peanut blanchers, nut butter mills, corn masa mills for tortillas and chips, and pellet puffing systems. The product line also features the modular M360 platform that allows customers to scale automation as production grows. A job shop division provides custom fabrication services. The Dallas facility employs approximately 1,000 people, though exact floor space and annual output figures are not publicly disclosed.

Horn serves snack food manufacturers of all sizes, from smaller regional processors to global corporations. Its equipment is used for popcorn, roasted and coated nuts, Japanese-style peanuts, nut butters, corn-based snacks, and puffed pellets. The company's customer base spans the broader food processing sector, with particular depth in nut and snack applications.

The company attributes its differentiation to a century-old commitment to craftsmanship — using high-quality components, thoughtful design, and no shortcuts — backed by an unrivaled service pledge to fix issues quickly and provide ongoing technical support. The 2024 acquisition by PROBAT, another family-owned firm, was framed as a cultural fit that would strengthen both organizations through vertical integration and shared expertise.

about:
KYOCERA AVX, headquartered in Fountain Inn, South Carolina, traces its origins to 1922 when Radiola Wireless was established in New York City. Through a series of transformations—including the Aerovox era and the founding of Electrical Reactance Corp in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina—the company was formally incorporated as AVX Corporation in 1972. A 1990 merger with Japan’s Kyocera Corporation led to full ownership by Kyocera in 2020, and the business adopted the KYOCERA AVX brand in 2021.

The company designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of advanced electronic components, including capacitors, connectors, antennas, filters, crystal devices, sensing and control modules, diodes, varistors, fuses, inductors, couplers, thermal management solutions, thermistors, resistive products, and SAW devices. It operates several dozen research, development, and manufacturing facilities across more than 15 countries, supported by a global workforce of over 15,000 engineers, researchers, technicians, and specialists. Core capabilities include custom design services and laser direct structuring (LDS) manufacturing.

KYOCERA AVX serves customers in automotive, aerospace, medical, industrial, military and defense, consumer electronics, 5G and IoT, aviation, automation, renewables, and high-temperature applications. Its components are engineered for mission-critical systems ranging from automotive power supplies and satellite communications to medical implants and industrial sensors.

The company emphasizes a “zero defect” quality culture, continuous improvement of its quality management systems, and an employee-first philosophy that it credits for its collaborative innovation. Its stated mission is to innovate technologies and products for tomorrow’s solutions while delivering superior customer satisfaction.

about:
Able Coil & Electronics was founded in 1969 in Bolton, Connecticut, by Ken Rockefeller to address a growing demand for high-quality coil winding and assembly services. The company remains under Rockefeller family leadership, with Steven Rockefeller serving as president since 2020, when the business expanded into a new state-of-the-art facility alongside its original location, bringing total manufacturing space to more than 40,000 square feet.

The company specializes in custom wire-wound electromagnetic products, including coil assemblies, transformers, encapsulated and toroidal assemblies, fine-wire assemblies, inductors and chokes, cable and connector harnesses, and electro-mechanical assemblies. Its vertically integrated operation covers manual and multi-spindle CNC winding (#4–#56 AWG), automated selective soldering, precision injection over-molding, vacuum pressure impregnation, epoxy and silicone encapsulation, selective conformal coating, and in-house 3D printing and tooling. Testing capabilities include HI-POT up to 20 kV, inductance, capacitance, resistance, impedance, turns ratio, and statistical process control. Annual output reaches millions of components, from prototype to full-scale production.

Able Coil serves aerospace and defense (avionics, satellite communications, radar), commercial and industrial, telecommunications, laser, medical (including imaging equipment), and music and audio markets. Customers range from OEMs requiring mission-critical reliability to commercial programs needing high-volume consistency.

The company differentiates itself through vertical integration that controls design, winding, assembly, and testing under one roof; collaborative engineering support with 3D modeling and rapid prototyping; flexible manufacturing from single units to millions; and a commitment to tight tolerances, complex geometries, and stringent environmental requirements without compromise.

Decker, who began his German-car journey with a 1986 VW Jetta GLI, expanded the catalog to include turbos and complete RS4 body kits before selling the company in 2006 to Bill Spencer, owner of Hartmann Wheels, a brand that has supplied the U.S. market since 1978. Spencer, a three-decade veteran of German-car tuning, now owns and directs Achtuning.

The company specializes in the distribution and installation of performance parts for Audi, Volkswagen, BMW, and Porsche vehicles. As an authorized distributor for brands including APR, Centric Parts, Girodisc, H&R, Hartmann Wheels, and StopTech, Achtuning stocks a high volume of inventory on site for immediate shipment or installation. The Redmond facility houses offices, a retail showroom, a main warehouse, and a seven-lift installation bay. A staff of ten, each of whom owns and works on German cars, handles everything from basic oil changes to brake service, scheduled maintenance, and full performance builds.

Achtuning serves the European car enthusiast community through its physical storefront and an international location in Korea. The company sponsors regional events and online forums such as Audizine, QuattroWorld, and VWVortex, and is a proud sponsor of Audi Club Northwest, the largest Audi enthusiast group in the Pacific Northwest. Customers range from individual owners seeking maintenance or upgrades to shops sourcing OEM-quality components.

The business distinguishes itself by maintaining deep stock levels — 40,000 square feet of storage by one account — and by testing parts on its own vehicles, both street and track, before offering them for sale. As an authorized distributor, Achtuning guarantees genuine products without knockoffs or factory “B-Stock,” backed by manufacturer technical support.

about:
AdvancedPCB traces its roots to 1977 when Advanced Printed Circuit Technology (APCT) was founded in Santa Clara, California. The company now operates under the unified AdvancedPCB name following a 2024 merger of APCT, Advanced Circuits, and San Diego PCB Design. Its headquarters are in Aurora, Colorado, with additional manufacturing and engineering sites in Santa Clara, Chandler, Anaheim, Maple Grove, and Orange County.

The company provides end-to-end printed circuit board solutions, including design services, fabrication, and assembly. Its fabrication capabilities span quick-turn prototypes, standard multilayer boards (up to 10 layers), advanced high-density interconnect (HDI) and ultra-HDI designs (up to 40 layers), flex and rigid-flex circuits (1–6 layer flex, 4–22 layer rigid-flex), RF/microwave boards, and heavy-copper constructions. Assembly services cover turnkey, kitted, and partial fulfillment with lead, RoHS, and no-clean solder options, and no minimum volume requirements. Turnaround times range from same-day to four weeks, with manufacturing turns as fast as 24 hours.

AdvancedPCB serves aerospace and defense, telecommunications and networking, medical technologies, industrial and robotics, and data center, networking, and storage markets. Its boards meet IPC Class 2 and Class 3 standards, and the company holds AS9100 quality certification for aerospace programs. Customers include engineers and product teams developing everything from satellite systems and medical devices to cloud infrastructure and robotic controls.

The company emphasizes domestic manufacturing as a differentiator, operating multiple U.S. facilities to protect intellectual property, ensure ITAR compliance, and enable faster collaboration. It also offers a hybrid model with vetted offshore partners for non-ITAR, high-volume production. Free design-for-manufacturability (DFM) checks, proprietary design software (PCB Artist), and a “strive to say yes” service philosophy round out its value proposition.

The company emphasizes competitive pricing, timely delivery, and a commitment to meeting customer needs faster and more affordably than competing manufacturers. This value proposition, combined with the expanded capabilities from the Group CBS partnership, forms the basis of its market positioning.

Product Identification customers span life sciences, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, industrial manufacturing, food and beverage, and cosmetics. Test & Measurement systems are deployed in aerospace and defense, power and utilities, transportation, automotive, and general industrial applications. Customers include OEMs, commercial printers, brand owners, airlines, and defense contractors.

AstroNova emphasizes innovation, responsiveness, and technical support as its competitive edge. A passionate commitment to quality drives zero-defect manufacturing and continuous improvement, underpinned by compliance with ISO, AS9100, FAA, RoHS, WEEE, and REACH standards.

about:
Atlantic Semiconductor operates from Peabody, Massachusetts, where it has been supplying electronic components since 1995. The privately held company was established to provide authenticated, reliable parts to original equipment manufacturers and contract manufacturers.

The company maintains a 26,500-square-foot warehouse and a proprietary database, called the Matrix, that tracks more than 10 million electronic components and computer products. Beyond distribution, Atlantic Semiconductor runs an in-house authentication lab staffed by component engineers and certified quality inspectors. The lab performs a range of counterfeit-detection tests, including acetone and scrape tests, X-ray examination of bond wires and lead frames, parametric I‑V curve tracing for diodes and transistors, functional memory testing with Advin equipment, and bench testing of oscillators, switches, and relays.

Customers are primarily OEMs and contract manufacturers in the electronics, semiconductor, and computer industries. The company also partners with external test houses such as Semiconductor in Clearwater, Florida, and Custom Analytical in Salem, New Hampshire, to extend its analytical capabilities.

Atlantic Semiconductor says its differentiation rests on ISO 9001:2015 certification, a focus on counterfeit prevention, and a commitment to fast fulfillment and fair pricing. The firm’s stated goal is to provide superior service that fosters repeat business and continual improvement.

AutoPartSource serves the automotive aftermarket and light‑ to medium‑duty truck segments. The company also supplies emergency‑service vehicles and offers private‑label programs for brake pads and cabin air filters.

The firm emphasizes made‑in‑the‑USA production for its cabin air filters and highlights full‑line coverage engineered to OE form, fit, and function. Its differentiators include the zinc coating process, premium coated steel, and the ability to customize private‑label offerings for distributors.

The company employs approximately 1,800 people and serves as a regional hub for the Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, which connects more than 2,200 parts stores and 3,000 certified service centers throughout North America.

APH’s customer base includes independent auto parts retailers, professional repair shops, and heavy-duty truck service providers through its affiliation with HDA Truck Pride. The distributor supplies a broad range of aftermarket components for passenger vehicles and commercial trucks, emphasizing rapid fulfillment from its Midwest warehouses.

The company says its differentiation lies in a service-first culture — “Service is the difference” — backed by core values of integrity, continuous improvement, and community support. APH highlights its family ownership and long-term relationships with suppliers and store owners as key to its ability to say “yes” to customer requests and maintain consistent parts availability.

about:
BEI Precision traces its roots to 1862 when D.H. Baldwin founded the D.H. Baldwin Company in Cincinnati, Ohio, initially building pianos and later electronic organs. The optical encoder technology emerged from the development of "Tone Wheels" for organs, and the company now operates from Maumelle, Arkansas, where its manufacturing plant continues that legacy of precision.

The company designs and manufactures high‑precision optical encoders — housed and un‑housed (kit) designs, absolute and incremental, single‑turn and multi‑turn — as well as flight‑worthy pivot‑and‑jewel accelerometers, displacement sensors, and rotary optical scanners. All products are designed and manufactured in the USA, available in both ITAR‑controlled and EAR‑regulated configurations, and supported by a broad engineering network and robust supply chain for custom and sole‑source solutions.

BEI serves defense primes, aerospace OEMs, and government programs across air, land, sea, and space domains. Its encoders provide gimbal feedback for airborne ISR payloads, precision angular measurement for weapons targeting systems, and closed‑loop positioning in next‑generation combat vehicles. Accelerometers are deployed in fixed‑wing, rotary‑wing, and unmanned platforms for flight control and vibration monitoring, while optical scanners support EO/IR systems in ISR payloads, weapons sighting, and airborne surveillance.

A long heritage of sole‑source programs with defense primes and ITAR‑compliant domestic production underpin its position in mission‑critical sensing.

about:
Bay City Electric Works was founded in 1932 by Bob and Leola Norris as a small appliance repair shop on University Avenue in San Diego. The business became a Kohler generator dealer in 1962 and was appointed Kohler's distributor for San Diego and Imperial Counties in 1971. Ownership changed hands several times: in 1984 the assets were purchased by CDS Electric (Wilmer Spitzer, Wally Dier, Tom Claycomb); Tom Claycomb took full control in 1986. In 2007 Mark Loftin, Chuck Loftin, and Rodney Lee acquired the company, and in 2021 the Lee family — Rod & Kim Lee, Austin & Kara Lee, and Adrian Lee — bought 100 percent of the stock, making it a family-owned operation. The corporate headquarters moved to a 70-employee facility in Poway, California, in 2012.

Today the company operates as an authorized distributor for Kohler (now Rehlko) emergency standby generators, automatic transfer switches, and paralleling switchgear, as well as Bobcat industrial air compressors and portable generators. It maintains a multimillion-dollar parts inventory and provides 24/7 service, maintenance, and repair for all generator brands. Bay City also runs a rental fleet, offers application engineering and generator training for contractors and specifying engineers, and operates a 20,000-square-foot sales and service center opened in 2024 in Galt, California, to serve Northern California and Northern Nevada.

The customer base spans commercial, industrial, and residential sectors, including healthcare facilities, data centers, municipal agencies, and homeowners across California, Nevada, and Hawaii. Contractors and specifying engineers rely on the firm's application engineering support for design, installation, and safety compliance.

Bay City emphasizes a customer-centric philosophy — “The Customer Is At The Center Of All We Do” — and positions itself as the exclusive power systems supplier for its three-state territory, backed by over 90 years of continuous operation.

Bow Auto Parts, based in Bow, New Hampshire, has been a family-owned and operated supplier of used automotive parts since its founding in 1986. The business stocks a wide inventory of used engines, transmissions, axles, body panels, and thousands of other car and truck parts for domestic and import vehicles. Trained technicians pull each part, inspect and test it, then enter it into a digital inventory system before it becomes available for sale. The operation runs from a climate-controlled facility with a staff of around 70 employees, supporting fast order fulfillment across the region.

Bow Auto Parts serves auto repair shops, dealerships, body shops, and individual vehicle owners throughout New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Maine, Vermont, and Rhode Island. Its catalog covers brands such as Ford, GM, Honda, Toyota, BMW, Ram, Jeep, Nissan, and many others, with fitment confirmed down to engine size, transmission type, and trim variations.

The emphasis on original manufacturer parts, rigorous testing, and climate-controlled storage aims to give customers a reliable, cost-effective alternative to new or aftermarket components.

Bradford Woodworking was founded in 1980 by master craftsman Brad Smith on the Worcester, Pennsylvania farm where he was raised. The business began as a one-man operation on his family farm, turning everyday farm tools into distinctive furniture pieces.

Each piece is made by Smith using traditional woodworking techniques such as lathe turning and hand joinery, with select components like tractor seats sourced from Amish forges. The workshop operates on the original farm property, though the company also fulfills wholesale orders through the Faire marketplace.

Bradford Woodworking serves both retail customers and wholesale buyers, with products ranging from entryway benches and dining stools to baby furniture and kitchen accessories. Retailers stock their goods via Faire Direct, while individual clients commission custom pieces directly with Smith.

The brand’s differentiation lies in its “farm fresh furniture” concept—repurposing agricultural implements into heirloom-quality pieces. Smith has stated that the venture began from a desire to transform utilitarian farm tools into objects that are “something special and much greater than their parts.”

Customers span homeowners, mill shops, subcontractors, general contractors, restaurant owners, and electrical contractors across the Denver metro area from Colorado Springs to Fort Collins, with the ability to ship nationwide.
